WELCOME TO THE HART PLAIN INFANT SCHOOL
Together we will aim high!
A Letter From
Every child deserves to belong to a school that enables them to thrive and succeed. Here, at Hart Plain Infant School, our vision is to aim high in all that we do and together we will:
Try our best to get success.
Stay happy and safe.
Show respect to our community.
Just over 60 years ago, Kennedy had a dream to land on the moon. With determination, creative, scientific and mathematical thinking and with a strong team to support him: he achieved. Just like Kennedy, young children dream big things. We will inspire your child to reach for their moon.
Learning is not just something that happens at school, it is lifelong. Here at Hart Plain Infants, our Learning Heroes help everyone to build strong learning habits. Please read more about Eddie Effort, Casey Courage, Harley Happy, Robbie Respect and Immy Integrity.
The vehicle that drives learning is the curriculum. We endeavour to promote a love of learning through a rich, engaging and ambitious curriculum which is personalised to the needs and interests of our children. An absorbing curriculum should have secret doors in familiar worlds that children did not know existed.
Please telephone the school office and book your family tour. We look forward to seeing you soon.
Mrs Sharon Peckham
Headteacher

Welcome to Space Station One
Mrs Ellis, Miss Rowley and I are looking forward to being part of your Year 1 journey this year, and what a year we have planned for you!
Our big topic question for this half term is “How can we help Percy to look after our community and world?”
Percy the Park Keeper has written to us as his park has been destroyed. He has asked us to design and make new playground equipment for him so children can enjoy to play in his park once again! We will be going to the local park to look at all the equipment and discover what materials are used for each one. We will also be learning some important key vocabulary.
In Maths we will be learning about Place Value within10, Addition and Subtraction within 10 and Shape and Pattern.
In English we will be reading The Three Little Pigs and Goldilocks and the Three Bears. Here, we will use our Oracy skills to retell the story from our illustrated story maps and plans!
Children need to bring their book bags to school every day as we may read with them on different days. There also maybe be important letters for you to see, so please check them with your child every day after school. Please keep reading with your child at home and filling in their bookmark and completing their Missions. The children love it when they move up!
PE is on a Monday with Mr H so children need to come into school wearing their PE kit. PE will also be taught on a Wednesday where they will be practicing their changing skills, so a PE kit needs to be in school on that day.
If you have any questions or concerns, please speak to one of us at the door.
Thank you for your continued support,
Mrs Edwards and Mrs Ellis and Miss Rowley

pageCache.text:
Welcome to Space Station Two
Year 2 – Meerkat Mail Adventure!
Get ready for an exciting half term as Year 2 join Sunny the meerkat on an adventure around the world!
Our learning journey will begin with the wonderful book Meerkat Mail, which will inspire us to explore different continents and discover what makes each place special. In English, we will follow Sunny’s travels and develop our descriptive and writing skills, building towards an exciting final outcome: writing a postcard from Sunny’s perspective, telling everyone about his adventures and the places he has visited. Our Geography learning will take us on a journey across the globe as we learn to identify and locate the seven continents and five oceans, discover the Equator, and explore how our world is organised. In Science, we will learn about different animals and explore what they need to survive, including food, water, air and shelter. We will investigate how animals are suited to their environments and compare the needs of different species.
In Maths, we will be securing our understanding of place value, using practical resources and engaging activities to help us understand the value of each digit in a number. We will also become budding chefs in DT, designing and making our very own delicious apple crumbles!
Our RE learning will be brought to life with a special Diwali Day, where we will explore the story, traditions and celebrations associated with the Hindu festival of lights. It promises to be a busy, exciting and adventurous half term!

pageCache.text:
Welcome to the website of Hart Plain Infant School. The Governors are proud to be part of the school and I would like to let you know about us and our role within the school.
Our Governors play an active part in our school.
What are Governors?
The Governing Body is responsible for the strategic management of the school. This includes overseeing the delivery of the curriculum, the upkeep of the school environment and the financial aspects of running the school.
The Governing Body comprises up to 10 people. This includes school employees, including the Head Teacher but also a number of volunteers from various backgrounds bringing a wide range of skills and experience. These represent parents, the local community and the Local Authority and bring a variety of skills and experiences to contribute to the strategic management.
All the Governors share a passion to enhance the children’s learning and to support the work of the school.
What Do Governors do?
The Governing Body has many legal responsibilities for the school. As well as the longer term strategic planning it is also required to ensure that effective policies are set to ensure the smooth running of the school.
To do this it operates through everyone attending half termly meetings where all matters are discussed including school finance, curriculum matters, policy setting and school updates.
Governor Details and Register of Interests 2026-2027 and Attendance 2025-2026
Mrs Denise Hooper is the school’s Safeguarding Governor.
Statutory documents and School’s Policies are available for inspection in the School Office.
Chair of Governors
Our governors are led by the Chair, Carole Roberts. Carole brings a wealth of knowledge with her. If you would like to contact her directly you can do so via email at chairofgovernors@hartplain-inf.hants.sch.uk
New Governors
Governors are appointed for a period of office of 4 years. Vacancies do come up from time to time. Vacancies for Parent Governors will be advertised through the school.
If you are interested in becoming a Governor, or know somebody who may be, then please email the Chair of Governors at chairofgovernors@hartplain-inf.hants.sch.ukhttps://607200b5-eb3b-4f5a-b8c0-fd0ebd310f51.usrfiles.com/ugd/607200_d42f6f6afb7f41fcb82206328a59007c.pdf

📅 Parent Meetings and Reports at Hart Plain Infant School
At Hart Plain Infant School, we value strong partnerships with families. Together, we can ensure your child has the best possible start to their learning journey.
Each term, you will be invited to a Parent’s Evening where you can meet with your child’s teacher to:
Discuss your child’s progress and achievements
Talk through their next steps in learning
Share ideas on how we can work together to support them
This is a great opportunity to ask questions and hear more about your child’s day-to-day experiences in school.
At the end of the summer term, we celebrate your child’s learning through a special Family Consultation meeting.
A video conference where your child talks with their class teacher about their achievements
A link to the video so you can watch and enjoy it again at home
A written summary of your child’s attainment and progress
Your child’s books to see how their learning has grown throughout the year
These meetings are a special time to reflect on how far your child has come—and to feel proud together!
If you ever have questions or concerns outside of these times, please don’t wait—we’re always happy to talk. You can speak to your child’s class teacher, make an appointment via the school office, or contact us directly.
Year Group emails are:
EYFS@hartplain-inf.hants.sch.uk

yeartwo@hartplain-inf.hants.sch.uk

School dinners
Hot school meals are available to every child each school day. These are free of charge to parents and are ordered in class during morning registration.
If your child would like a hot meal but will be late to school, please ensure you telephone the school office on 023 9226 2511 before 9:15am.
Note that orders after this time cannot be taken and parents will be required to provide a packed lunch for their child.
Our school caterers are owned and managed by Cleverchefs. They focus on providing balanced and nutritious meals, using fresh ingredients, cooked on site each day.
Packed Lunches
Children may bring a packed lunch from home but please remember:
Food should be in a named plastic container
Only one treat (crisps or a packed lunch chocolate bar)
No high sugary drinks or fizzy
No nuts or products with nuts
Milk and Fruit
Milk is offered daily to all pupils under the age of 5. This is free to parents.
Most children stop having milk at school after five, but they’re very welcome to continue while in Early Years. If you’d like your child to receive milk, simply register with Cool Milk
Cool Milk handles the payments and delivers the milk directly to school. Just make sure you pay by 5pm on Tuesday for milk to start the following week.
All children are offered a free piece of fruit or veg mid morning, however you may provide your own fruit or healthy snack if you prefer.

The colours of the school uniform are jade, white and black. Only jade jumpers/cardigans can be worn in school. These can be purchased from supermarkets and do not have to be school branded.
Please make sure that all belongings are marked clearly with your child’s name. Our uniform is:
White polo shirt – Required
Black or grey skirt, pinafore, shorts or trousers – Required
Jade school sweatshirt/cardigan or jade jumper/cardigan – Required
Jade/white summer dress – Optional
Black sensible shoes (no heels)
No jewellery except stud earrings.
Physical Education (PE)
PE uniform is a white T-shirt and black shorts . Please provide a plain, warm track suit for PE during the winter. Children will need to keep their PE uniform in a small shoe bag marked with your child’s name, which is kept in school during term time. For safety reasons, children should not wear earrings on PE days.
School Shop
School sweatshirts and cardigans are available to purchase via Arbor. Please see the school office if you require support to log in.
The stock items and prices are as follows:
Preloved uniform is available to purchase from the school office for a cash donation. We have a variety of items in a range of sizes, all in great condition.

pageCache.pageTitle: Security & Safety | Parents | Hart Plain Infant School
pageCache.text:
It is everyone’s responsibility to ensure that school is a happy and safe place for every child to learn and flourish.
If you have any concerns about the security and safety of the school then please notify the school office.
Visitors and helpers are asked to sign our visitor’s book and will be provided with a visitor pass.
Smoking is not permitted anywhere on the school site.
Dogs of any age or size are not permitted on the school site.
Parents are not permitted to drive on the school site.
If someone different is collecting your child. Please telephone the school office and provide their details. We will ask the person you have nominated to collect your child to provide identification.
As well as welcoming families into school each morning on the gate, Mr Griffiths, Site Manager, keeps the school site safe.
At Hart Plain Infant school, we teach the children to be happy and safe just like Harley Happy. Mrs Peckham is the Lead Designated Safeguarding teacher. Mrs Ellis and Mrs Stevens are deputy safeguarding officers. We are always available to talk to you.
Read more about the legal duties we uphold to keep your child safe
Keeping Children Safe in Education

pageCache.pageTitle: Sickness And Medication | Parents | Hart Plain Infant School
pageCache.text:
Our learning hero Harley Happy teaches us that we need to come to school so that we can make strong relationships with our friends and teachers and feel ‘Harley happy and safe’. Sometimes children will be poorly. Below is a guide to help you decide whether to send your child to school:
If your child is fit to return to school but still requires medication, please deliver the medicine to the main office, where you will be asked to complete a consent form. If you prefer, you may come into school to give medication to your child. We can administer prescribed medicines and Calpol.
Mrs Ellis is our school attendance officer. If your child is sick, you must telephone the office between 8:30 and 9am and discuss this. Mrs Ellis will support you in ensuring your child returns to school as quickly as possible.

pageCache.pageTitle: Travelling to School | Parents | Hart Plain Infant School
pageCache.text:
The roads outside of school get very congested. Please walk or cycle to school if you can. Please use the dedicated crossing areas to help you arrive at school safely.
Mr Griffiths will be at the school gate to welcome you every morning. The parking inside the main driveway is for staff only and should not be used by parents. However, in exceptional circumstances, e.g. if your child is unwell and you have been called to school, you may use parking facilities within the grounds.

pageCache.pageTitle: SEND | Our School | Hart Plain Infant School
pageCache.text:
SEND at Hart Plain Infant School
Hart Plain is a two form entry thriving, community focused Infant school. We are passionate about securing positive outcomes for each individual pupil, and recognise the importance of working with parents and support services. We support all pupils to ‘Aim High’ so that each child is fulfilling their own potential.
To find out more about how we support pupils with SEND, please click here.
To view our SEND Policy, please click here.
What is a School Information Report?
As of 2014, every school has had to publish a School Information Report outlining what the school can offer its pupils who have been identified with Special Needs and Disabilities. The report must be published annually and be linked in with the local authority’s report which is available by clicking on this link. To view Hart Plain Infant School's report, please click here our SEND report
Our SENCo is Mrs Leanne Ellis who can be contacted directly by email: inclusion@hartplain-inf.hants.sch.uk
